title: Virus-like particles enable targeted gene engineering and pooled CRISPR screening in primary human myeloid cells - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A Gladstone-UCSF/Stanford/Broad consortium reports a virus-like-particle (VLP) toolkit that delivers Cas9, base-editor and CRISPRoff ribonucleoproteins into primary human monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells at high efficiency without the viability and transcriptional damage caused by nucleofection, and pairs VPX-lentiviral sgRNA delivery with VLP-delivered Cas9 protein (SLICeVLP) to run the first pooled loss-of-function and Perturb-seq screens in primary human macrophages, converging on TNFAIP3 (A20) as a master brake whose ablation makes HER2 CAR macrophages more cytotoxic and resistant to suppressive repolarization. Note: the captured record contains the abstract, figure titles and the ten Extended Data figure legends only — the main body sits behind 'This is a preview of subscription content', so the raw record's paywalled=false flag understates access restriction and most headline efficiency percentages are not in the captured text.

themes.theme: VLP delivery unlocks primary myeloid cells

insights.claim: Virus-like particles deliver CRISPR ribonucleoproteins into primary human monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells with high editing efficiency while preserving both cell viability and innate immune responsiveness, removing the long-standing engineering bottleneck in myeloid cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Myeloid cell therapy has been delivery-constrained; a working non-electroporation delivery chassis expands the addressable cell-therapy target set beyond T and NK cells.
insights.quote: Here we present a virus-like particle (VLP)-based toolkit that delivers diverse CRISPR editing modalities to human monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells with high efficiency while preserving viability and innate immune responsiveness.

insights.claim: A single VLP chassis supports three distinct CRISPR modalities in primary human macrophages — nuclease gene knockout, base editing and CRISPRoff epigenetic silencing — meaning the delivery platform, not the payload, is the reusable asset.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Platform-style delivery IP that is payload-agnostic is worth more than any single edit; watch which delivery companies license the particle rather than the editor.
insights.quote: VLP-mediated delivery of ribonucleoproteins supports gene knockout, base editing and epigenetic silencing.

insights.claim: Nucleofection, the incumbent method for CRISPR RNP delivery into primary myeloid cells, fails to maintain viability of human primary monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells, whereas VLP-mediated editing does — the comparison is run head-to-head across multiple nucleofection buffers.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cell yield is the dominant cost driver in autologous manufacturing; a delivery method that avoids nucleofection-induced attrition changes the unit economics of myeloid cell products.
insights.quote: VLP-mediated gene editing, but not nucleofection maintains viability of human primary myeloid cells.

insights.claim: Two structurally different particle systems are used in parallel — Cas9EDVs quantified by HIV p24 ELISA and Cas9-eVLPs quantified by MMLV p30 ELISA — and both were dose-titrated across monocytes, day-4 M-CSF macrophages, immature dendritic cells and mature dendritic cells for B2M knockout.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Two independent viral backbones both working reduces single-vector platform risk and gives licensees an alternative if one lineage hits IP or immunogenicity problems.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2d — Monocytes (Day 0), macrophages (Day 4 of differentiation

insights.claim: Cas9 protein delivered by eVLPs into primary human macrophages and T cells was tracked in whole-cell lysates by ELISA alongside editing at days 2, 5, 9 and 12, characterizing the delivery as transient hit-and-run rather than persistent nuclease expression.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Transient protein exposure is the regulatory argument against off-target accumulation; it is the same case Beam and Prime make for RNP/LNP over integrating vectors.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 2a — Primary human macrophages or T cells were treated with AAVS1-targeting Cas9-eVLPs

insights.claim: VLP-edited primary human macrophages retained core innate immune functions across four independent assays — phagocytosis of pHrodo-labeled E. coli at two doses, NLRP3 inflammasome IL-1beta release after LPS priming plus nigericin, STING-agonist (diABZI) driven CXCL10 secretion, and LPS/IFN-gamma cytokine release.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Delivering a viral-derived particle to an innate immune sensor cell without blunting its sensing is the key technical risk; clearing it is what makes myeloid engineering commercially plausible.

insights.claim: Bulk RNA-seq gene set enrichment showed nucleofected macrophages upregulating xenobiotic metabolism and oxidative phosphorylation pathways after LPS and IFN-gamma stimulation, a stress signature that Cas9EDV-treated cells did not share, so electroporation perturbs macrophage biology beyond the intended edit.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Screen and therapy data generated by electroporation in myeloid cells may carry a method artifact; a reason to discount prior nucleofection-based myeloid datasets.
insights.quote: Upregulation of genes involved in Xenobiotic metabolism and Oxidative Phosphorylation pathway observed in nucleofected cells after LPS/IFN-γ stimulation.

insights.claim: Transcriptional effects of editing were benchmarked by projecting GSVA scores onto four established monocyte/macrophage subpopulation signatures — CD14APC (antigen processing and presentation), CD14CTX (chemotaxis and suppressive cytokines), CD14IFL (inflammatory) and CD14ISG (interferon-stimulated) — rather than relying on gross viability alone.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A reusable release-criteria framework: any myeloid manufacturing process can be scored against these four axes to prove it did not silently repolarize the product.

insights.claim: Combining Cas9EDV particles with adeno-associated virus-delivered donor template enables site-specific integration of large DNA sequences by homology-directed repair in primary human macrophages, a cell type that is post-mitotic and therefore historically considered HDR-refractory.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Site-specific knock-in, not just knockout, is what allows a targeted CAR insertion in macrophages — the same step that moved CAR-T from lentiviral randomness to defined-locus products.
insights.quote: Combined with adeno-associated virus-mediated donor delivery, this approach enables site-specific integration of large DNA sequences by homology-directed repair.

insights.claim: Correct knock-in junctions for CLTA-GFP and RAB11A-GFP in primary human macrophages were verified by in-out PCR across at least four human donors and confirmed by nanopore sequencing of the template-genome junctions, not merely by GFP fluorescence.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Junction-level sequencing evidence is the bar regulators apply to knock-in products; its presence here raises the translational credibility of the platform.

insights.claim: Knock-in efficiency in primary human macrophages was probed pharmacologically using 1 uM of the NHEJ inhibitor M3814 or the TMEJ inhibitor ART588 across four human donors, indicating that DNA repair-pathway steering with small molecules is being used as a tunable lever on HDR outcomes in non-dividing cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Repair-inhibitor cocktails are a separately licensable layer in cell-therapy manufacturing; M3814 and ART588 are named, clinically-adjacent tool compounds worth tracking.

insights.claim: The Cas9EDV plus AAV6 knock-in workflow also worked in the THP-1 and U937 human myeloid cell lines, where sorting the top 5% of GFP-positive cells produced stable lines with homogeneous GFP-RAB11A expression.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Line-level reproducibility means the method is deployable as a research-tools product immediately, ahead of any therapeutic timeline.

themes.theme: Base editing and break-free silencing in macrophages

insights.claim: ABE8e-loaded eVLPs and cytosine base editor eVLPs carrying an sgRNA targeting a B2M splice site both produced base edits in primary human macrophages, with A-to-G edits, off-target C-to-T conversions and residual indels each quantified separately by next-generation sequencing across four human donors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Reporting bystander C-to-T from an adenine base editor and indel rates alongside on-target edits is the purity disclosure buyers of base-editing platforms should demand.

insights.claim: CRISPRoff-eVLPs targeting the transcriptional start sites of CD81, CD45 and CD14 reduced both transcript levels by RNA-seq and surface protein by flow cytometry in primary human macrophages across four donors, demonstrating heritable-style gene silencing without cutting DNA.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Break-free silencing sidesteps translocation risk in multiplexed products — the main safety objection to nuclease-based multi-edit cell therapies.

insights.claim: The same ABE-eVLP reagents targeting the B2M splice site were validated in primary human T cells across two donors in parallel with macrophages, showing the particle system is not myeloid-specific and carries directly into the established CAR-T manufacturing setting.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Cross-lineage generality widens the licensing market for the particle from a niche myeloid tool to the whole allogeneic cell-therapy stack.

themes.theme: SLICeVLP: making pooled screens possible in primary macrophages

insights.claim: SLICeVLP decouples the two halves of CRISPR by delivering the sgRNA as a VPX-containing lentiviral vector (which integrates and provides the barcode readout) while delivering Cas9 as protein inside engineered VLPs, solving the reason pooled screens were previously impractical in primary human macrophages.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A reusable architecture: any cell type that resists nuclease expression but tolerates lentiviral guides can now be screened, which is the growth path for functional-genomics service providers.
insights.quote: We developed SLICeVLP, which pairs sgRNA delivery by VPX-lentivirus with Cas9 protein delivery by engineered VLPs, and used it for pooled loss-of-function and Perturb-seq screens in human macrophages.

insights.claim: VPX inclusion in the lentiviral vector is the enabling variable for macrophage transduction — flow plots compare HER2CAR lentiviral transduction with and without VPX — reflecting VPX's role in degrading the SAMHD1 restriction factor that blocks reverse transcription in myeloid cells.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: SAMHD1 is the specific molecular reason myeloid gene therapy lagged T cells; anyone building myeloid vectors needs a VPX-equivalent workaround and the IP around it.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 6a,b — Schematic representation showing production of VPX-containing lentiviral vectors

insights.claim: The SLICeVLP workflow was control-hardened by treating sgRNA-transduced macrophages with empty or scramble-sgRNA-loaded Cas9EDVs, confirming that editing specificity comes from the lentivirally delivered guide rather than any guide carried in the particle.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Guide-swap artifacts have discredited earlier primary-cell screen platforms; explicit scramble controls are what make this screen data trustworthy.

themes.theme: Screen hits: TNF, CD80 and the PD-L1 link

insights.claim: Pooled loss-of-function screens in primary human macrophages, run in cells from two human donors and analyzed with MAGeCK under both median and non-targeting-control sgRNA normalization, identified positive and negative regulators of TNF production and of CD80 surface expression.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: TNF and CD80 are the two output nodes that determine whether a macrophage product is inflammatory and T-cell-priming; a hit list for both is a target-discovery asset.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 7b,c — Scatter plot showing correlation between two biological replicates

insights.claim: Screen hits were re-tested one-by-one in arrayed format using Cas9-eVLPs against five positive and five negative regulators, with intracellular TNF staining after 50 ng/mL LPS for 5 hours and NGS genotyping across six human donors — an unusually deep validation layer for a primary-cell screen.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Six-donor arrayed validation with genotyping is the standard that separates a durable target list from a screen artifact; use it as a benchmark when diligencing rival functional-genomics claims.

insights.claim: Knocking out CD274 (PD-L1) in primary human macrophages was followed by measuring both surface PD-L1 and total CD80 and PD-L1 by immunoblot under basal and LPS plus IFN-gamma stimulated conditions, tying the CD80 screen directly into the PD-L1:CD80 cis-heterodimer axis that gates CD28 costimulation.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If PD-L1 levels on myeloid cells set available CD80, checkpoint-blockade response variability may be a myeloid-costimulation problem, not only a T-cell one.

insights.claim: SLICeVLP was extended to Perturb-seq in primary human macrophages under both unstimulated and LPS-stimulated conditions, with per-guide knockdown significance assessed against target gene expression level and perturbation clusters scored by GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Single-cell transcriptomic screens in primary innate immune cells under stimulation is a genuinely new dataset class; the GEO deposits are a free look at a competitive moat.
insights.quote: SLICeVLP enables Perturb-seq to analyze gene-regulatory networks in human macrophages.

insights.claim: The screen and Perturb-seq raw sequencing data were deposited to the Gene Expression Omnibus under accessions GSE327424 and GSE327644 and all custom analysis code released publicly at github.com/mangochiral/Macs_CRISPR_2026, so the underlying target lists are independently minable rather than proprietary.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Open data means the discovery layer is not defensible IP here — the defensible asset is the particle and the patent, not the hit list.

insights.claim: Both the TNF and CD80 screens converged on TNFAIP3 (the A20 deubiquitinase) as a central regulator of inflammatory polarization in primary human macrophages, making it the paper's single named target rather than a diffuse hit list.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: TNFAIP3 is the myeloid analogue of the RASA2/REGNASE-1 T-cell edits that anchored Arsenal Bio-style programs; expect it in next-generation CAR-macrophage constructs.
insights.quote: We uncovered regulators of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and CD80 expression, converging on TNFAIP3 as a central regulator of inflammatory polarization.

insights.claim: TNFAIP3 ablation in primary human macrophages produced a proinflammatory state that resisted suppressive repolarization, meaning the edited cells hold their inflammatory phenotype against the immunosuppressive signals that normally convert tumor-associated macrophages into a pro-tumor state.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Resistance to TME-driven repolarization is the specific failure mode of CAR-macrophage therapy; an edit that fixes it is the value-creating step for that whole modality.
insights.quote: TNFAIP3 ablation drove a proinflammatory state resistant to suppressive repolarization and enhanced cytotoxicity in chimeric antigen receptor macrophages.

insights.claim: HER2CAR primary human macrophages with TNFAIP3 disrupted showed enhanced killing of mKate-positive SK-OV-3 ovarian cancer cells in five-day co-culture, with secreted cytokines measured at 6 and 24 hours across two human donors.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A concrete efficacy delta in a HER2 CAR-macrophage model, the same modality already in phase 1 for HER2-overexpressing solid tumors, gives an editable path to a differentiated second-generation product.

insights.claim: The enhanced killing by TNFAIP3-edited HER2CAR macrophages was interrogated with a 5 ug/mL anti-TNF antibody (adalimumab biosimilar) versus IgG isotype control at 96 hours, explicitly testing how much of the anti-tumor effect runs through secreted TNF.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If efficacy is TNF-dependent, patients on TNF blockers become a contraindicated population and cytokine-release toxicity becomes the dose-limiting risk to model in any IND.
insights.locator: Extended Data Fig. 10g — TNF antibody blocking assay

insights.claim: The same TNFAIP3 loss-of-function phenotype was reproduced without double-strand breaks by using TadCBEd cytosine-base-editor eVLPs to install a premature stop codon, with protein loss confirmed by immunoblot, giving a nuclease-free route to the therapeutic edit.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A break-free version of the value-creating edit is the clinically filable version; this is the step that makes the TNFAIP3 program IND-plausible rather than research-only.

insights.claim: HER2CAR surface expression on primary human macrophages was verified to be preserved across all experimental conditions in which Cas9EDV or CBE-eVLP particles were used to disrupt TNFAIP3, ruling out the trivial explanation that editing changed CAR density rather than macrophage biology.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Confirming the CAR is unchanged is what makes the efficacy gain attributable to the edit — the key control any licensee would demand.

insights.claim: Transcriptome-wide consequences of TNFAIP3 ablation in primary human macrophages were mapped by DESeq2 differential expression plus GSEA against both MSigDB KEGG and Hallmark gene sets, filtered at adjusted p < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change > 1.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A full transcriptional characterization of the edited product is the safety package a regulator will ask for; its presence shortens the diligence path.

insights.claim: The lead and corresponding authors state they are coinventors on a patent application covering this VLP myeloid engineering work, and two of them are scientific consultants for Site Tx, indicating the toolkit is already routed toward a named commercial vehicle rather than remaining an academic tool.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Track the patent family and Site Tx financings — the platform IP, not the published data, is where the value accrues.
insights.quote: H.J., P.D., A.M. and J.C. are coinventors on a patent application related to the work described in this manuscript. H.J. and J.C. are scientific consultants for Site Tx.

insights.claim: The captured article text stops at the abstract and jumps to a subscription prompt, so the main results section with headline editing efficiencies is not present; the quantitative detail available comes from figure titles and the ten Extended Data legends, which report donor counts (n = 2, 4 or 6 human donors) but not the percentage efficiencies claimed as 'high' in the abstract.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Any downstream model built on this record should not assume specific efficiency numbers; the record's paywalled flag understates the access restriction on the body text.
